claims.text: Homogenized Al0.7CoCrFeNi is a eutectic high-entropy alloy with a dual-phase lamellar FCC/B2 structure.
The initial Al0.7CoCrFeNi state exhibits strong-yet-brittle behavior.
The initial lamellar structure has incoherent interfaces prone to interfacial cracking.
HPHT treatment in a hexahedron-anvil apparatus at 6 GPa and 1473 K for 2 hours can simultaneously increase strength and ductility.
The proposed HPHT treatment transforms the FCC/B2 lamellar structure into a hierarchical microstructure.
The proposed HPHT treatment converts incoherent interfaces into coherent interfaces.
Coherent interfaces facilitate preferential dislocation transfer from the softer FCC phase to the harder B2 phase.
Preferential dislocation transfer from FCC to B2 reduces stress concentration.
The hierarchical microstructure activates dislocation motion, stacking faults, microbands, and twins.
Activation of multiple deformation mechanisms accommodates plasticity and promotes homogeneous strain distribution.
The HPHT-treated alloy is expected to reach approximately 1150 MPa strength.
The HPHT-treated alloy is expected to reach approximately 36% tensile ductility.
HPHT treatment is expected to shift fracture behavior from catastrophic interfacial cracking to distributed microcracking.
Conventionally arc-melted and cast or homogenized eutectic high-entropy alloys exhibit room-temperature brittleness and limited ductility.
The synergistic improvement requires formation of the hierarchical microstructure under the specified 6 GPa and 1473 K HPHT conditions.
Lower-pressure treatments or conventional HIP are not expected to produce the same hierarchical pattern or strength-ductility improvement.
The quantitative strength and ductility improvements may vary with process control and alloy variability.
